guards.name: A change to the gate's own rules must be approved by a person before a release
guards.evidence: Enforced (preventive): the CI job policy-change-check holds the release with POLICY_CHANGE_REQUIRES_REVIEW when a protected path changed, and the release jobs wait for a person to start approve-policy-change, which refuses automation accounts. Audited (detective): every main pipeline is checked afterwards. The Witness itself has no such check and its decisions are unchanged. 19 pipeline(s) carry a policy-change record; no guard is missing on a recorded main run. Limit: removing the guard in a merge request is only caught afterwards (needs a pipeline execution policy, Owner).

guards.name: A repair merge request may only change training code
guards.evidence: Yes, as an early signal: the repair-scope CI job runs on merge requests from repair/ branches and reads its rules from the target branch. It is not tamper-proof; protected branches and required review are the real control (docs/SETUP.md). Last recorded guard failure: !7, guard rejection.

policy.guard_limit: Preventive limit: a merge request that deletes the guard from .gitlab-ci.yml runs without it in its own pipeline. Stopping that needs a GitLab pipeline execution policy, which only an Owner can set. So every main pipeline is also audited afterwards: a release-eligible run that changed a protected path but has no policy-change record is listed under Needs attention as a missing guard.
